extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: The Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD) is a synthetic texture dataset containing 246,285 images across 56 texture classes. It was generated using Stable Diffusion with texture-specific prompts constructed from combinations of descriptors across five categories (texture, artistic, spatial, enhancer, color). The dataset was refined through a three-stage process consisting of frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP score filtering to ensure high quality, diversity, and alignment with prompts. PTD is intended to support texture-based research including texture bias analysis, interpretability, and robustness in machine learning.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel (University of Wisconsin-Madison)
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, B., & McDaniel, P. (2025). On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Texture images were generated synthetically using the Stable Diffusion text-to-image model. Prompts were constructed by combining descriptors across five categories (texture, artistic, spatial, color enhancer, color) in standard English adjective order, yielding 96,768 unique prompts. Five images were generated per prompt using Stable Diffusion from HuggingFace, producing 483,840 images before refinement. Images flagged as NSFW by Stable Diffusion's safety filter were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Up to 60% of initial generated images were flagged as NSFW by Stable Diffusion's safety filter, despite using benign prompts. Flagged images were excluded from the dataset and regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images generated via Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace using texture-specific prompts. The 47 texture class starting list was derived from the Describable Textures Dataset (DTD), expanded with 9 additional classes sourced from texture word lists.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged as NSFW by Stable Diffusion's safety filter were regenerated to maintain 5 images per prompt. The safety filter was temporarily disabled during analysis to record flagged images, though flagged images were excluded from the final released dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering using Fourier transforms to remove object-like images, retaining the top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values per class; (2) Patch variance filtering dividing images into 50x50 pixel non-overlapping patches and filtering out the bottom 20% with lowest mean patch variance per class; (3) CLIP score filtering removing the bottom 20% of images with lowest CLIP scores per class to ensure prompt alignment. The final refined dataset contains 246,285 images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted on 900 unique images (pre-refinement) where 9 participants each evaluated 100 randomly-ordered images. For each image, participants answered two questions: (1) overall quality of the image, and (2) how well the image represents the provided descriptor. Ratings were on a 1-5 scale.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mean quality and representative scores were computed across images at different stages of refinement. Each refinement step showed improvement: overall 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness. Patch Variance and CLIP refinement contributed the most to quality and representativeness increases, respectively. Participant comments were also collected on observed trends.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 human rating per image (100 images per participant, 9 participants, 900 unique images total)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion (HuggingFace), CLIP (for CLIP score computation), Inception model (for Inception scores), Fourier transform-based frequency analysis
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work highlights the need for refined NSFW filters that can better handle abstract or texture-based content, as the authors found benign texture prompts were disproportionately flagged as NSFW despite containing no explicit content. The dataset contributes to advancing interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Fourier analysis indicated textures in the dataset are not biased towards a certain frequency and capture frequencies found in real data (DTD). However, quality varies across texture classes—textures appearing in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) tend to have better scores than more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted). Certain descriptor pairings (e.g., 'muted' with subtle textures) yield lower quality images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Generated images may occasionally contain object-like rather than texture-like content, necessitating the refinement process. Structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) are harder to generate well than complex natural textures. The Stable Diffusion NSFW safety filter is overly sensitive to texture data, flagging up to 60% of benign texture images. Some symmetric images requested are not actually symmetric, and color descriptors sometimes alter backgrounds.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Texture-based research including measuring texture bias in object classification models (e.g., via Texture Object Association Values/TAV metric), uncovering texture-object associations, studying model interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning. Can be used for training, testing, and validation in texture-related ML tasks.
